artifactType.reason: SETTLED 1Sep26 by project decision: PART. GD-PIP gained a real sub-member and declared junction on 30Aug26 (the outer pipe and its root), which had pushed it toward Assembly under the literal Sec.3.2 test and left this field open with candidate=Assembly. The decision is that an internal sub-member does not make an artifact an assembly when it is not independently placeable: a PiP outer sleeve is concentric with and fabricated onto the inner pipe, never positioned as a separate component in a layout. Supersedes the previous open state.

free.name: x_interior_R
free.meaning: AXIAL POSITION, relative to centre_x, of the junction where the outer sleeve meets the inner pipe on the RIGHT. Its presence is what creates a right-hand outer member.

free.name: x_interior_L
free.meaning: Same on the LEFT. At least one of the two is required -- a bulkhead with neither has no outer member at all.

free.name: OD_outer
free.meaning: OUTSIDE DIAMETER of the outer sleeve. REQUIRED -- the outer pipe is a real structural member with its own contact surface and cannot be inferred from the inner pipe.
free.note: no pipe-relative default — would guess a diameter into every contact result
free.default: four NOMINAL SIZES above the line (nps_step_up(OD_pipe, 4))
free.defaultNote:
DEFAULTED since 5Sep26; previously required. FOUR NOMINAL SIZES larger, NOT OD + 4 inches -- the two differ for every line below NPS 14, since nominal size is not the OD there (NPS 6 is 168.3 mm, not 152.4). On a 16 in line the sleeve is NPS 20 = 508.0 mm. The earlier code comment refused a default on the grounds that no basis existed and inventing one would put a guessed diameter into every contact result; that reasoning stood until a basis was supplied.
CLEARANCE INTERACTION, found on introducing the default: the sleeve must clear the INNER thick body, and NPS+4 leaves only 19.3 mm of radial room against a default inner body (t_comp = 2.5*t_pipe gives OD_comp = 469.4 mm on a 16 in line). So t_outer must be under about 19 mm for the default pairing to build -- 25 mm is rejected. The default OD is not generous, and t_outer keeps no default of its own because a wall does not follow from a diameter.

free.name: t_outer
free.meaning: WALL THICKNESS of the outer sleeve.
free.stillRequired: No default. Deliberate: nothing was supplied for it, and a wall thickness does not follow from a diameter. Note it is CONSTRAINED by OD_outer via the clearance check -- see OD_outer.defaultNote.

derived.name: halfExtent
derived.expr: halfExtent = same as edes:GD-TT (inherited). The OUTER sleeve may reach further: outer stations sit at x_interior_L/R and the sleeve ends, so the component extent is the wider of the two.
derived.meaning: HALF the component's axial footprint. extent = (centre_x - halfExtent, centre_x + halfExtent). Needed to place this component adjacent to another -- see edas:shared#/chaining.
derived.verifiedAt: the instance shown in verifiedWith below

geometry.nodes: 6 inner (weldL/taperL/bodyL/bodyR/taperR/weldR -- conMid explicitly filtered out, see assemblyFeatures.noMidConnector) + 2 per outer member. VERIFIED LIVE at 8 nodes with one interior node set, 10 with two.
geometry.lines: 5 inner (one per consecutive station pair) + 1 per outer member, own line id. VERIFIED LIVE at 6 lines with one interior node set. The inherited builder derives this count from the station list rather than hard-coding it, so the filtered station list produces 5 not 6.
geometry.junctions: [outer-pipe root -> pipeline], per side. DECLARED not inferred — root x is caller-supplied, no coordinate coincidence to detect it by.
geometry.contact: outer pipe wins wherever it overlaps the inner pipe axially — lowest surface. contact_at fixed 30Aug26: previously returned inner surface over outer span despite docstring claiming refusal.

sectionClaim.verified: section_at() returns Section(OD=0.4694) at centre_x on STD_PIPELINE, VERIFIED LIVE; contact_at() returns a real Contact.
sectionClaim.consequence: Same as edes:GD-VLV -- may not overlap another section-claiming component, and an explicit header chain must be split around it and welded on both sides.
sectionClaim.twoWeldChains: NOTE this component sits in TWO chains, and only one of them is the pipeline. The INNER pipe (weldL/weldR) carries the header line and is what ils_builder.weld_chain() joins. The OUTER sleeve ends (outLEnd/outREnd) are a SEPARATE weld chain for the pipe-in-pipe outer line; a neighbour mated to those would be joined to the annulus, not to the pipeline.
sectionClaim.inTheWeldChain: GD-PIP is in ils_builder.INLINE_CODES via its inner pipe.

assemblyFeatures.status: the mate points an adjacent component ties to are weldL/weldR, inherited unchanged from edes:GD-TT (PipBulkhead subclasses TaperedThickBody) and VERIFIED LIVE 1Sep26. Same NIB caveat as GD-TT applies: weldL/weldR sit past L_NIB from the taper toe, so a join naming taperL/taperR would place the neighbour too close by that length.
assemblyFeatures.outerPipeNotChainMatable: CORRECTED 1Sep26. This field previously stated that the outer-pipe stations 'are NOT chain mate points' and described outREnd as 'the outer pipe's own free end' -- WRONG for the End stations. outLEnd/outREnd are real AssemblyFeatures that accept a W (weld) connection: they are where the PiP line's own outer pipe is welded onto the bulkhead sleeve. They are now listed in slots above. What remains true, and was the defensible half of the original claim, is that they do not continue the HEADER line: a chain join along the pipeline runs weldL -> weldR through the inner pipe, and a neighbour mated to outREnd would be joined to the annulus, not to the pipeline. So there are TWO distinct weld chains through this component -- inner (weldL/weldR, the header) and outer (outLEnd/outREnd, the sleeve) -- and confusing them is the error the original wording was reaching for but overstated.
assemblyFeatures.strictnessCaveat: whether these are OAMFeatures in NISTIR 7436's strict sense or merely Features depends on whether the component is mated in a given layout -- see edes:shared#/frameworks OAM.usedButLooser.AssemblyFeature candidacy.
assemblyFeatures.junctionsAreNotFeatures: outLJn/outRJn are NOT AssemblyFeatures and are deliberately absent from slots. They are the internal junctions where the outer sleeve meets the inner pipe -- declared node-merges within one component, not interfaces to a separate artifact. Per edes:shared#/frameworks OAM.narrowerOnPurpose.junction, a junction is directional and internal; an AssemblyFeature is an interface to another Part. Nothing external mates at outLJn/outRJn.
assemblyFeatures.noMidConnector: GD-PIP has NO mid-body connector station, by explicit decision 1Sep26. It briefly inherited one: conMid was added to TaperedThickBody._station_xs for GD-TP/GD-TT and propagated here through super(), taking this component from 8 nodes to 9 as an unassessed side effect. PipBulkhead now overrides _station_xs to filter it out by id. Reason: a PiP bulkhead already has its attachment point -- the outer member's free end (outLEnd/outREnd), where a Boss attaches -- and a second competing attachment mid-body is not part of this component's definition. VERIFIED LIVE back at 8 nodes with one interior node set.

behaviourDerived.outerLoadPath: IMPLEMENTED 30Aug26 as component_spec.PipBulkhead.outer_load_path. Rule: external load on outer pipe -> outer pipe's OWN end nodes (structural distribution) -> junction -> pipeline, by stiffness ratio. Two hops, not one — PIPE_ELEMENT on contact_at means reaction is on the OUTER element, not already on the pipeline.
behaviourDerived.mass: NO catalogue archetype exists for GD-PIP — no independent oracle, unlike GD-TP/GD-TT

usedInLayouts.note: Back-links to worked layouts containing this component, generated mechanically from the layout library on 1Sep26 -- not hand-written, so they cannot drift from it by authoring error, though they WILL go stale if the library changes and this is not regenerated. Their purpose is placement guidance: this file describes what the component IS and what its own constraints are, but says nothing about where along a header to put one or what to put either side of it. A worked archetype answers that by example. paramsUsed are the archetype's own values verbatim; anchors are published table rows that override them.
usedInLayouts.absent: no archetype in standard_ils_layouts.json contains this component. That is not necessarily a gap in the library -- it may simply never have been the subject of a published study -- but it does mean there is no worked layout to copy parameter values or placement from, so an LLM configuring one has this component's own constraints and nothing else to go on.

placement.centre_x: REQUIRED to place the component. EDES gives NO guidance on the value. No archetype in the layout library contains this component, so there is NO worked precedent to take a value from -- query.

inputsRequired.ifMissing: Anything listed as required, having no default, and not supplied by the person must be QUERIED. Do not assume a value and do not carry one over from a worked example -- a precedent shows what was once chosen, not what this case needs.
